findings.tests: UI-11 / WAL-11 display limitation (backend projection itself passes)
findings.title: Wallet shows yesterday’s spending as “Spent today”
findings.reproduction: On the positively labelled disposable E2E DB only, set guild-buyer daily_spent=300 and daily_spent_on to UTC yesterday. Open /#wallet, select guild-buyer and reload. GET /api/guilds/guild-buyer/wallet independently.
findings.expected: Today’s visible completed spend is 0.00 G; raw inspector retains yesterday’s 300 with its date. Reading must not alter stored history.
findings.actual: Wallet visibly shows Spent today 3.00 G. GET wallet returns daily_spent=0; SQL retains 300 and yesterday’s date. Reproduced in both custom browser sessions and reviewer SQL test. No spending-limit bypass observed.
findings.action: Use current-day wallet projection for Wallet/Overview, or project with the observation’s UTC day while keeping dated raw inspector data. Add a stale-day UI regression.

findings.title: Reciprocal purchases acquire wallet locks in opposite order and deadlock
findings.reproduction: Run tools/run_independent.py against this exact checkout. The retained source copy adds only reviewer_independent_test.go. Create a rare listing owned by seller and another owned by buyer. Launch buyer buying seller’s item and seller buying buyer’s item concurrently. A test-only wallet wrapper waits after each real Spend has locked its buyer row; then lets both real Earn calls proceed. This deterministically schedules a naturally possible interleaving without changing application SQL or domain code.
findings.expected: Valid reciprocal operations complete through consistent multi-wallet lock order or a bounded transaction retry; failed attempts must roll back.
findings.actual: TestReviewerReciprocalPurchasesDoNotDeadlock fails: one service operation returns ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01), the other succeeds. SQL total gold=30000, audit rows=2, sold orders=1. Rollback/money conservation hold. HTTP 500 follows from handler mapping by source inspection; HTTP deadlock response was not separately executed.
findings.action: Acquire all participating wallet locks in a deterministic order, or deliberately retry the entire transaction on 40P01/40001 with bounded attempts. Retain rollback/idempotency guarantees. Review cross-auction two-wallet paths too.
findings.status: Open; deterministic counterexample preserved; no production source patched.

findings.title: Mobile wallet audit region cannot receive keyboard focus
findings.reproduction: With wallet audit rows present, open /#wallet at 390×844 in Chrome. Run axe-core 4.11.1 WCAG2 A/AA and WCAG2.1 AA scan; inspect .table-wrap.
findings.expected: A horizontally scrollable audit table has an accessible keyboard scrolling path, with suitable region naming/focus behavior.
findings.actual: Repeated scans flag scrollable-region-focusable, impact serious, target .table-wrap. Audit table has overflow content with no focusable descendant/tabindex. Desktop scan has zero violations. Skip link, main focus, mobile page width, navigation and refresh checks pass. No screen-reader evaluation or complete WCAG certification performed.
